name: Oberon
explanation: An eight-voice polyphonic analog synthesizer modelled control-for-control on the original 1979 Oberheim OB-X (OB-X Owner's Manual, 2nd Ed., 2nd Printing, June 1980). Each of the eight voices is a complete synth with two VCOs, a single SEM-derived 2-pole (12 dB/oct) resonant low-pass filter, two full ADSR envelopes and a VCA. This is the FIRST OB-X, NOT the later OB-Xa: it has ONLY the 2-pole filter (no selectable 4-pole slope), a smoother SEM-flavoured resonance and no filter-envelope-to-oscillator routing. CONTROL: polyphonic PORTAMENTO, UNISON (low-note-priority detuned stack), OSC 2 DETUNE (flat/sharp of OSC 1) and MASTER TUNE. MODULATION: one LFO (SINE / SQUARE / SAMPLE&HOLD, ~0.1-20 Hz) with a FREQUENCY DEPTH routable to OSC 1 / OSC 2 / FILTER and a PULSE-WIDTH DEPTH routable to OSC 1 / OSC 2. OSCILLATORS: OSC 1 and OSC 2 each have a continuous FREQUENCY control (per the manual, ~11 o'clock = one octave up) plus independent SAW and PULSE waveform switches summed additively; a shared PULSE WIDTH control; SYNC hard-locks OSC 2 to OSC 1. FILTER: the classic OB-X mixer buttons select sources into the filter (OSC 1 on/off, OSC 2 off/half/full, NOISE on/off), FREQUENCY, RESONANCE, MODULATION (filter-env amount) and keyboard TRACK (100% or off). Two ADSR envelopes drive the Filter and the Loudness (VCA). Performance: PITCH and MODULATION levers (the mod lever fades LFO vibrato in), a programmable BEND RANGE, a stereo PAN SPREAD echoing the OB-X's per-voice pan pots, HOLD latch, VOLUME. Switch groups are bit-packed into single host parameters; the panel decodes and shows every individual switch. AUTO auto-tune, the 32-program cassette/programmer memory and CHORD memory transposition are host or hardware concerns and are out of scope.
